solution:
In each case the parent chain is numbered from the carbon of the carbonyl group (C-1 for an aldehyde), and the Greek letter \(\alpha\) denotes the carbon adjacent to \(\text{-CHO}\).

(i) \(\alpha\)-Methoxypropionaldehyde: propionaldehyde is \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\); the \(\alpha\)-carbon is C-2, so the methoxy group goes there.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OCH}_3)\text{-CHO}\)

(ii) 3-Hydroxybutanal: \(\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CHO}\)

(iii) 2-Hydroxycyclopentane carbaldehyde: a cyclopentane ring whose C-1 carries \(\text{-CHO}\) and whose C-2 carries \(\text{-OH}\).

(iv) 4-Oxopentanal: \(\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHO}\) (C-1 is the aldehyde, the keto group is at C-4).

(v) Di-sec. butyl ketone: the sec-butyl group is \(\text{-CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\), so two of them flank the carbonyl.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3)\text{-CO-CH(CH}_3)\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\), i.e. 3,5-dimethylheptan-4-one.

(vi) 4-Fluoroacetophenone: \(4\text{-F-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CO-CH}_3\) (a benzene ring bearing \(\text{-COCH}_3\) with \(\text{-F}\) at the para position).

(i) Friedel-Crafts acylation: benzene is acylated by propanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous \(\text{AlCl}_3\).
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCl} \xrightarrow[\text{CS}_2]{\text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{HCl}\)
Product: propiophenone, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (1-phenylpropan-1-one).

(ii) A dialkylcadmium reacts with an acyl chloride to give a ketone; both alkyl groups are transferred.
\((\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2)_2\text{Cd} + 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \rightarrow 2\,\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CdCl}_2\)
Product: 1-phenylpropan-2-one (phenylacetone).

(iii) Acid-catalysed hydration of an alkyne in the presence of \(\text{Hg}^{2+}\) follows Markovnikov's rule; the enol formed tautomerises to the carbonyl compound.
\(\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+},\ \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3\)
Product: propanone (acetone).

(iv) Etard reaction: chromyl chloride oxidises the methyl group of an arene to \(\text{-CHO}\) (via a chromium complex hydrolysed by \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}\)); the ring nitro group is unaffected.
Product: 4-nitrobenzaldehyde, \(4\text{-O}_2\text{N-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-CHO}\).

All four compounds have nearly the same molecular mass (44-46), so the order is fixed by intermolecular forces alone.

\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (propane) is non-polar and has only weak van der Waals forces, so it boils lowest. \(\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3\) (dimethyl ether) is weakly polar and has dipole-dipole interaction, but its oxygen bears no hydrogen, so no hydrogen bonding. \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}\) (ethanal) has a much larger dipole moment because of the strongly polar carbonyl group, so its dipole-dipole attraction is stronger than that in the ether. \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\) (ethanol) has an \(\text{-OH}\) group and is extensively associated by intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so it boils highest.

Increasing order of boiling points:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 < \text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3 < \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\)

Reactivity towards a nucleophile increases as the carbonyl carbon becomes more electrophilic and less crowded. Alkyl groups both hinder the approach of the nucleophile (steric effect) and push electron density onto the carbonyl carbon (+I, electronic effect), so each extra or larger alkyl group lowers reactivity; an electron-withdrawing group raises it.

(i) Ethanal has one methyl group, propanal one ethyl group, and the two ketones have two alkyl groups each, with butanone the more hindered of the pair. Increasing order:
Butanone \(<\) Propanone \(<\) Propanal \(<\) Ethanal

(ii) Acetophenone is a ketone (two bulky electron-releasing groups) and is the least reactive. Among the aldehydes, the \(\text{-CH}_3\) of \(p\)-tolualdehyde releases electrons (+I, +R) and lowers reactivity relative to benzaldehyde, while the \(\text{-NO}_2\) of \(p\)-nitrobenzaldehyde withdraws electrons (-I, -R) and raises it. Increasing order:
Acetophenone \(<\) \(p\)-Tolualdehyde \(<\) Benzaldehyde \(<\) \(p\)-Nitrobenzaldehyde

Each reaction is a nucleophilic addition of an ammonia derivative to the carbonyl group followed by elimination of water, giving a \(\text{>C=N-}\) compound.

(i) Cyclopentanone \(+\ \text{NH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^{+}}\) cyclopentanone oxime \(+\ \text{H}_2\text{O}\); the ring carbon that carried \(\text{=O}\) now carries \(\text{=N-OH}\).

(ii) Cyclohexanone \(+\) 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine \(\rightarrow\) cyclohexanone 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone \(+\ \text{H}_2\text{O}\); the ring carbon now carries \(\text{=N-NH-C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2\). This is the orange-red 2,4-DNP derivative.

(iii) \(\text{R-CH=CH-CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{N-NH-CO-NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^{+}} \text{R-CH=CH-CH=N-NH-CO-NH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
The semicarbazone forms at the aldehyde group; the carbon-carbon double bond is not attacked.

(iv) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=N-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
Product: the substituted imine (Schiff's base) N-ethyl-1-phenylethanimine.

The carboxyl carbon is always C-1 of the parent chain; when \(\text{-COOH}\) is attached to a ring the compound is named as a cycloalkanecarboxylic acid.

(i) \(\text{Ph CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\): a three-carbon chain ending in \(\text{-COOH}\) with a phenyl group on C-3.
3-Phenylpropanoic acid

(ii) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CHCOOH}\): four carbons in the chain, double bond between C-2 and C-3, methyl on C-3.
3-Methylbut-2-enoic acid

(iii) A cyclopentane ring with \(\text{-COOH}\) on C-1 and \(\text{-CH}_3\) on the adjacent carbon:
2-Methylcyclopentane-1-carboxylic acid

(iv) A benzene ring with \(\text{-COOH}\) at C-1 and nitro groups at both ortho positions (C-2 and C-6) and at the para position (C-4):
2,4,6-Trinitrobenzoic acid

(i) Ethylbenzene: side-chain oxidation of an alkylbenzene by hot alkaline permanganate removes the whole side chain except the carbon attached to the ring.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KMnO}_4\text{-KOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOK} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\)

(ii) Acetophenone is a methyl ketone, so it gives the haloform reaction; the methyl group leaves as iodoform.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{NaOH}]{\text{I}_2} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{CHI}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\)
(Hot alkaline \(\text{KMnO}_4\) followed by acidification serves equally well.)

(iii) Bromobenzene: Grignard route, which adds one carbon.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Br} \xrightarrow[\text{dry ether}]{\text{Mg}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{CO}_2\ (\text{dry ice})} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOMgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\)

(iv) Phenylethene (styrene): the carbon-carbon double bond of the side chain is cleaved oxidatively.
\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH=CH}_2 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KMnO}_4\text{-KOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOK} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\)

An acid is stronger when the carboxylate ion left after loss of the proton is better stabilised. Electron-withdrawing groups (-I) disperse the negative charge and strengthen the acid; the effect falls off sharply with distance from the carboxyl group.

(i) Fluorine is strongly electron-withdrawing, whereas the methyl group of acetic acid releases electrons.
Stronger: \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCO}_2\text{H}\)

(ii) Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, so its -I effect is greater.
Stronger: \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCO}_2\text{H}\)

(iii) Both acids carry one fluorine, but in \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHFCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}\) it sits on the \(\beta\)-carbon (C-3) while in \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}\) it sits on C-4. The inductive effect weakens rapidly along the chain, so the nearer fluorine wins.
Stronger: \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHFCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}\)

(iv) \(\text{-CF}_3\) is strongly electron-withdrawing (-I) while \(\text{-CH}_3\) is electron-releasing (+I, hyperconjugation), so the trifluoromethyl compound gives the better-stabilised carboxylate.
Stronger: \(p\)-trifluoromethylbenzoic acid, \(\text{F}_3\text{C-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-COOH}\)
